name: Ride a motorbike or scooter
blurb: This one starts with a licence and formal training, not a video. Once trained, the core skills are counter-steering, smooth throttle and reading traffic as if you are invisible.
gear: The legally required training and licence for your country
A helmet plus proper protective gear, always
steps: Do the legally required training. This is not a skill to self-teach, and the training is what insurers and the law require.
Learn slow-speed control first: clutch, rear brake and throttle together for turns tighter than any car could manage.
Learn counter-steering — pushing the bar on the side you want to turn towards — which is how bikes actually steer above walking pace.
Learn threshold braking with both brakes, progressively, in a safe environment.
Learn road positioning and defensive riding: assume every driver has not seen you, because often they have not.
Wear full gear every ride, and take an advanced course once you have a season behind you.
tips: Target fixation is the classic killer: you go where you look, so look at the escape route, not the hazard.
The first six months carry the highest risk. Build experience gradually rather than buying a powerful bike immediately.
proof: You hold the licence, ride a mixed route confidently, and can do a slow-speed U-turn within a lane.
